text:
Use the Zoom Workplace app
Using the app rather than the web is significantly easier and has the benefit of better quality streaming for audio and video.

Go to https://zoom.com, click the ‘Meet’ menu, and choose ‘Download App’




Zoom menu with ‘Download app’ circled in red

title: Classroom Critical Incident Questionnaire
text:
The Classroom Critical Incident Questionnaire (Brookfield, n.d.) is a metacognitive tool you can use to help you reflect on your own experience as a learner in a classroom (analog or digtal). Being aware of your own experience as a learner is a powerful method of coming to know how you want to show up as a teacher.
The questionnaire consists of a few questions that you can answer in just a few minutes.

title: Classroom Critical Incident Questionnaire
text:
The Classroom Critical Incident Questionnaire
Please take about five minutes to respond to the questions below about this week’s class. If nothing comes to mind for any of the questions just leave the space blank. At the next class we will share the group’s responses with all of you. Thanks for taking the time to do this. What you write will help us make the class more responsive to your concerns.

At what moment in class this week did you feel most engaged with what was happening?

At what moment in class this week were you most distanced from what was happening?

What action that anyone (teacher or student) took this week did you find most affirming or helpful?

What action that anyone took this week did you find most puzzling or confusing?

What about the class this week surprised you the most? (This could be about your own reactions to what went on, something that someone did, or anything else that occurs).

Record your responses on your blog, but please do not mention specific people by name.
Use the category #cciq.

title: About Colin
text:
Hi everyone, I’m excited to be teaching EDCI 336 and I’m looking forward to getting to know each of you!
I am a PhD Candidate in Educational Studies at UVic researching technology-integrated assessment in higher education. My work explores the intersection of the purposes of assessment, duty of care, technology acceptance, and assessment design and theory. I am currently analyzing data for the third of three papers comprising my dissertation.
I taught educational technology in K-12 in BC, Alberta, and Japan between 2000 and 2010 and led technology-integrated teams in instructional design in higher ed and have taught courses at the undergraduate and graduate level in technology-integrated learning as well as transformational blended learning. I was most recently the Director of Technology Integrated Learning and Assessment at a small university in British Columbia where I supported faculty and learners in using technology to make sense of the world around them.
I live in West Kelowna, on the traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Syilx people, and I spend a bunch of my spare time on my bicycle, walking my dog, or doing cool stuff with my wife. We have three kids: one is a police officer in Abbotsford, where he lives with his wife and 2 boys, one is a nurse in Surrey living in Maple Ridge with her husband and twin boys, and the third is just starting his first year of university, studying Human Kinetics.
Contact and further info at cmad.land.
